metaDescription: Six 80V cordless lawn mowers compared by deck width, drive type and pack size, with clear advice on which yard and budget each one fits.
expertTake: The Greenworks 80V self-propelled 21 inch with a 4.0Ah pack is the best all-round pick, with the 8.0Ah version for anyone who wants more mowing per charge. The Greenworks 80V push mower is the value pick for flat ground. Anyone with steep terrain or several acres should skip battery walk-behinds.
introParagraphs: An 80 volt mower is the high end of the walk-behind cordless range. It trades a heavier pack and a higher entry cost for more sustained torque in thick grass and a bigger deck than the smaller platforms offer.
Voltage is only the label for the battery family. Deck width, drive type and pack capacity decide how long you mow and how much effort it takes, so this guide ranks the lineup by those factors.

products.name: Greenworks 80V 21in Self-Propelled, 4.0Ah
products.description:
This is the balanced mower of the 80V line. A brushless motor drives a 21 inch steel deck, and a rear-wheel variable-speed drive carries the machine so your arms only steer. The listing claims about half an acre from a 4.0Ah pack, which is a realistic figure for a flat lawn in dry grass.

The tradeoff is that self-propel draws from the same pack as the blade. The 4.0Ah pack stores roughly 288Wh at 72V nominal, so a thick lawn and a drive system will use it faster than the push version of the same mower. Against the 8.0Ah self-propelled Greenworks in this lineup, you save money but give up half the stored energy.

Expect a straightforward ownership. The deck is steel, the blade is a standard replacement, and the LED headlight helps with evening mowing.
products.bestFor: Lawns up to half an acre with a gentle slope.
pros: Rear-wheel variable-speed drive reduces slope effort
Brushless motor lowers heat and wear
LED headlight allows early or late mowing
Shares packs with other Greenworks 80V tools
cons: Single 4.0Ah pack is a hard limit on bigger lawns
Self-propel shortens runtime against the push version

products.name: Greenworks 80V 21in Self-Propelled, 8.0Ah
products.description:
The 8.0Ah pack is what separates this mower from the 4.0Ah version above. At 72V nominal it stores about 576Wh, double the smaller kit, so the self-propel drive does not eat the whole session. The deck is the same 21 inch steel design, with a push-button start and a 4-in-1 system that includes a turbo mode for leaf pickup.

The listing still quotes half an acre on a charge, which suggests the larger pack buys reserve rather than a bigger claim. In thick or wet grass that reserve is what keeps the mower from stopping early. The tradeoff is weight and recharge time, since a bigger pack takes longer to fill and adds heft to the mower.

Seven height positions cover seasonal changes. Because it uses the same Greenworks 80V platform as the other mowers here, the pack also works in matching tools. Owners with larger lawns or a habit of bagging will notice the difference most.
products.bestFor: Thick grass and lawns near half an acre.
pros: 8.0Ah pack roughly doubles stored energy
Self-propel drive without the usual runtime penalty
Four-in-one system adds a turbo leaf pickup mode
Seven height positions cover seasonal changes
cons: Larger pack takes longer to recharge and adds weight
Costs more than the 4.0Ah kit of the same mower

products.name: Greenworks 80V 25in Self-Propelled, 4.0Ah

specList.label: Coverage claim
specList.value: About three quarters of an acre

products.description:
The 25 inch deck is the reason to pick this mower. It cuts four more inches per pass than the 21 inch models, so an open lawn takes fewer trips, and the dual-blade system helps with mulching. Rear-wheel drive with variable speed carries the extra weight of the deck.

The listing claims about three quarters of an acre per charge, but that claim sits on the same 4.0Ah pack as the 21 inch self-propelled Greenworks. A wider deck loads the motor harder, so a thick lawn will not reach that figure. Tight beds and trees are harder to turn around with a 25 inch cut.

The aluminum handles and LED headlight are practical touches. Because the pack is shared with other Greenworks 80V tools, a second pack makes sense if you plan to mow an acre. Measure your garage bay first, since the deck is wide.
products.bestFor: Open lawns of half to three quarters of an acre.
pros: Wide 25 inch deck cuts fewer passes
Dual-blade system helps with mulching
Rear-wheel variable-speed drive handles the weight
LED headlight extends the mowing window
cons: Same 4.0Ah pack feeds a bigger deck load
Wide deck is harder to turn around beds and trees

products.name: Greenworks 80V 21in Push, 4.0Ah
products.description:
Without a drive system the whole pack goes to the blade. The same 4.0Ah pack that runs the self-propelled Greenworks therefore lasts longer here, and the mower weighs less to carry and store. A brushless motor and a 21 inch steel deck give it the same cutting width as the drive versions.

The cost is effort. On a flat lawn you will hardly notice, but on a slope or with a full bag you will push every step. Against the self-propelled 21 inch model, this is the right choice if your lawn is level and you value runtime over ease.

The LED headlight and steel deck are the same as the drive models, and the pack is shared with other 80V tools. Clean the underdeck after every mow and keep the pack indoors in cold weather.
products.bestFor: Flat lawns where runtime matters more than drive.
pros: All pack energy goes to cutting for longer runtime
Lighter machine is easier to carry and store
Steel deck matches the drive models
Same 80V pack fits other Greenworks tools
cons: No drive makes slopes and bagging tiring

products.name: PowerSmart 80V 21in Push, 6.0Ah
products.description:
The PowerSmart mower undercuts the Greenworks push model while carrying a larger battery. Its 6.0Ah pack is listed at 432Wh, which is half again the 288Wh of a Greenworks 4.0Ah pack. A brushless motor and a 21 inch steel deck complete a simple push design.

The maker claims up to 40 minutes of runtime and coverage near half an acre. That is a modest runtime for a lawn of that size, so keep expectations in line for thick grass. There is no self-propel, so slopes and bagging fall to your arms.

The real tradeoff is the platform. PowerSmart packs do not share with Greenworks tools, so you are buying into a smaller family with fewer accessories. Check that replacement packs are available before relying on it for years.
products.bestFor: Budget buyers with a flat half-acre lawn.
pros: Larger 432Wh pack than the Greenworks 4.0Ah kit
Brushless motor with a 21 inch steel deck
Lowest-cost route to an 80V push mower here
Includes battery and charger in one kit
cons: PowerSmart packs do not fit Greenworks tools
No self-propel and a modest quoted runtime

products.name: Greenworks 80V 21in Push, two 2.0Ah
products.description:
This older-format kit pairs two small 2.0Ah packs with a 21 inch push deck. Together they store about the same energy as one 4.0Ah pack, around 288Wh, and the listing claims up to an hour of runtime across both. A single lever sets five cutting heights and the 3-in-1 deck covers mulching, bagging and side discharge.

The second pack is the appeal. You can swap mid job without waiting on a charger, which suits a small lawn mowed in short sessions. The tradeoff is the pack count: carrying and charging two small packs is more handling than one 4.0Ah pack.

Because it is part of the Greenworks 80V family, the packs also fit larger mowers in this lineup. Treat this kit as a smaller-lawn machine and upgrade the packs later if your yard grows.
products.bestFor: Small lawns mowed in short sessions.
pros: Two packs allow a swap without waiting on a charge
Five cutting heights from a single lever
3-in-1 deck covers mulch, bag and side discharge
Packs fit larger Greenworks 80V mowers
cons: Two small packs mean more charging and handling
Only about 288Wh total, same as one 4.0Ah pack

buyingCriteria.explanation: An 80V label names a battery family, and it quotes the peak voltage, so nominal is closer to 72V. The PowerSmart and Greenworks mowers both say 80V yet use incompatible packs. Buyers often assume packs swap between brands. Decide on the platform first, then check what tools already share it.

Stored energy is volts times amp-hours. The PowerSmart 6.0Ah pack is listed at 432Wh, while the Greenworks 4.0Ah pack is about 288Wh and the 8.0Ah pack about 576Wh. Two 2.0Ah packs add up to the same 288Wh as one 4.0Ah pack. Compare watt-hours across brands.

A 21 inch deck suits most lots, as on the self-propelled and push Greenworks models. The 25 inch dual-blade Greenworks saves passes on open lawns but loads the motor and turns poorly around beds. Size the deck to your longest uninterrupted runs.

Self-propel draws from the same pack as the blade. The 4.0Ah Greenworks self-propelled kit will mow less than the push version of the same mower. The 8.0Ah kit hides that cost with reserve. Buy drive for slopes and bagging, not for flat ground.

The pack is the wear item, usually lasting a few hundred cycles. The Greenworks platform has wide stock, while the PowerSmart family is smaller. Confirm you can buy another pack before you rely on the mower for a decade. A shared platform also means a spare pack from a bigger kit can rescue an older mower.
A 4-in-1 deck like the 8.0Ah Greenworks adds a turbo leaf mode, but bagging pulls hard on any battery. Expect shorter runs with the bag on. Mulch if you mow often and only bag for leaves.

specDecoder.meaning: The peak voltage of a full pack. Nominal voltage, which sets sustained power, is lower, near 72V.
specDecoder.watchFor: Do not assume the PowerSmart 80V and Greenworks 80V share packs.

specDecoder.meaning: Capacity at a given voltage. Multiply by voltage to get watt-hours.
specDecoder.watchFor: The Greenworks 8.0Ah pack stores about double the 4.0Ah pack, so it is the larger reserve.

specDecoder.meaning: Width of the cut path. Wider decks cut more per pass but weigh more and load the motor.
specDecoder.watchFor: The Greenworks 25 inch adds four inches per pass over the 21 inch models.

specDecoder.meaning: A motor without carbon brushes, which runs cooler and wears slower.
specDecoder.watchFor: All six mowers here claim brushless, so the difference comes from the deck and pack.

specDecoder.meaning: Self-propel through the back wheels, which keeps traction when a bag adds weight at the rear.
specDecoder.watchFor: The Greenworks self-propelled models use it, but wet slopes can still slip.

howWeEvaluated.title: Platform fit
howWeEvaluated.description: We checked which battery family each mower belongs to and whether it shares packs with other tools. The PowerSmart does not fit Greenworks tools, so we flagged it as a smaller ecosystem. We also noted which kits include batteries. Platform fit matters most for owners who already have matching tools.

howWeEvaluated.title: Stored energy
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared pack capacity using amp-hours and the number of packs in each kit. The PowerSmart 6.0Ah pack is listed at 432Wh, while the Greenworks 4.0Ah pack is near 288Wh. We ranked mowers higher when reserve or swappable packs reduced downtime.

howWeEvaluated.title: Drive and slopes
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at drive type and how it suits terrain, using engineering logic and owner feedback patterns. The Greenworks self-propelled models use rear-wheel variable speed. We rewarded mowers that matched drive to the likely lawn.

howWeEvaluated.title: Deck and cut quality
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared deck width, height range and cut modes from the listings. The 25 inch Greenworks widens the cut, while the 8.0Ah kit offers seven heights. We favored a usable height range for seasonal changes.

howWeEvaluated.title: Ownership and upkeep
howWeEvaluated.description: We weighed storage, cleaning and parts support over several years. A 25 inch deck needs more garage space than a 21 inch one. We also considered how easy it is to find a replacement pack.

cards.label: Push
cards.text: All pack energy goes to the blade, so runtime lasts longer and the mower is lighter. The Greenworks 21 inch push and PowerSmart fit here. It suits flat lawns.

cards.label: Self-propelled
cards.text: Drive reduces effort on slopes and with a bag, but draws from the same pack. The Greenworks 4.0Ah and 8.0Ah self-propelled kits fit here. It costs some runtime.

howToChoose.note: Flat ground should push. Slopes or bagging justify drive.

howToChoose.subheading: Small Packs vs One Big Pack

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A large pack, a brushless motor and a deck that is not oversized. Thick or wet grass drains energy fast, so reserve matters more than headline coverage. A turbo or high-lift mode helps clear clippings.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The Greenworks 80V 21in Self-Propelled with the 8.0Ah pack is the best fit because it pairs drive with about 576Wh of reserve and a turbo mode. The 25 inch model loads the motor harder in thick grass.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You have a lawn near half an acre, thick grass or a slope. The Greenworks 8.0Ah self-propelled kit gives the reserve to finish without a stop. Pay for energy before deck width.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: Your lawn is flat and small. The PowerSmart push or the Greenworks 4.0Ah push mows it without a drive system. Add a second pack only if one runs flat.

maintenance.why: Wet clippings trap moisture and corrode steel decks. A plastic scraper clears buildup safely.
A dull blade tears grass and pulls more current from the pack. Balance it after sharpening to avoid vibration.
Lithium packs age faster in extreme temperatures. Store them at a partial charge in a dry room.
Self-propelled models rely on rear traction. Worn tread reduces drive on slopes.
Dirt causes voltage drop and false low-battery cutoffs. Use a dry cloth.

faq.q: Is 80V better than 60V for a mower?
faq.a: Voltage only names the platform. Stored energy, deck design and motor matter more, so compare watt-hours and the deck rather than the voltage number.

faq.q: How much should I budget for an 80V mower?
faq.a: Push kits cost less than self-propelled kits, and bigger packs cost more. The PowerSmart push sits at the low end, while the Greenworks 8.0Ah self-propelled kit sits near the top. Count the pack and charger. Bare comparisons mislead, so price the full kit.

faq.q: How long will an 80V mower last?
faq.a: Brushless motors and steel decks can last many seasons with basic care. The battery is the wear item and usually fails first. Confirm replacement packs are available.

faq.q: Does a bigger Ah rating mean a stronger mower?
faq.a: No. Amp-hours raise runtime, not blade power. The Greenworks 8.0Ah and 4.0Ah self-propelled models cut with the same motor and deck.

faq.q: Can I use Greenworks batteries in a PowerSmart mower?
faq.a: No. Packs sharing a voltage label are not interchangeable across brands. Stay inside one platform.

faq.q: Can I leave the battery in the mower over winter?
faq.a: Remove it and store it indoors at a partial charge. Cold garages and hot sheds shorten pack life.
